answers.explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol: simple because it's short text commands.
EHLO is the extended hello. HELO is the original and gets no list.
MAIL FROM: is the envelope sender, and bounces go there.
One RCPT TO: per recipient, each with its own reply.
A lone dot. Lines in the message that start with a dot get an extra one (dot-stuffing).
Dot-stuffing doubles a leading dot, and the receiver removes one.
VRFY lets spammers harvest valid addresses, so most servers refuse it or give a vague answer.
It upgrades the same connection to TLS, then the client says EHLO again.
